title: Phase 3 scope and resumability remediation
confirmation: Implementation and shipping require a new exact-SHA256 approval receipt for these amendment bytes.
reason: Independent code review found that required service identity verification, document/indexer contract coverage, generated OpenAPI artifacts, telemetry dependency declaration, and resumable migration mechanics require paths omitted from the original Phase 3 plan.
acceptance_criteria: Every accepted service assertion is bound to an active Web-owned service identity with matching actor ID, issuer, and signing-key ID.
Service assertions use Ed25519 with a per-service private key and Web-owned public key; rotation replaces the active key and immediately rejects tokens signed by the prior key.
Configured service and system identities are validated against the Web-owned registry at startup; non-Web services never query local databases for Web-owned identity tables.

Historical conversion is defined in one migration, executed by a separate top-level CALL migration, commits each 10000-row batch independently, and can resume after forcing the dirty CALL version back to the procedure-definition version.
Shared audit callbacks contain no repository-owned reflection adapter and continue to support batch creates.
Document/indexer tests assert actor attribution on relational writes and actor metadata on OpenSearch writes.
Verification evidence reports blockers and substitutions accurately and does not claim completion before all gates pass.
out_of_scope: New actor types or generalized identity frameworks

principles.kiss: Use one Web-owned registry contract and PostgreSQL procedures rather than duplicate identity tables or an additional identity subsystem.
principles.yagni: Add only service/system verification calls, resumable migration boundaries, and required document actor propagation.
principles.single_ownership: Web owns identity records; each migration version and each writer owns one explicit state transition.
principles.explicit_contracts: Actor IDs, issuer, signing-key ID, ownership, timeout, and invalid responses are explicit.
principles.fail_safe: Registry unavailability, invalid identity, missing actor, migration interruption, and projection failure reject or stop safely.
principles.observability: Counters are required for successful writes by actor type and service, missing actors, unknown actor writes, projection lookup failures, authentication actor-cache hits, authentication actor-cache misses, conversion rows processed, user-classified rows, unknown-classified rows, failed conversions, and remaining rows. Safe logs accompany missing actors, projection failures, authentication lookup failures, and each conversion batch/table summary, including actor type and non-secret actor ID where an actor exists. Operators record migration duration, lock waits, WAL growth, disk usage, replica lag, and cleanup status for every database.
principles.least_privilege: The registry response exposes only the active service public key needed for signature verification or a boolean system-ownership result; it never exposes private keys, credentials, or complete identity records.
principles.reversibility: Before cleanup, interrupted backfills are rerunnable and actor-capable binaries can roll back while additive columns remain. Legacy-column removal is the irreversible boundary and requires restoring the complete four-database backup set.

risks: Web registry availability becomes an authentication dependency for internal service requests.

Migration version renumbering is allowed only after git-history and environment evidence confirms every affected Phase 3 migration is unshipped; otherwise append corrective versions and retain existing numbers.
Generated SDK repositories require explicit nested commits before the root gitlinks can preserve delivery.
nested_repository_delivery: Record each nested repository starting SHA, remove unrelated changes from the RFC-owned diff, commit generated contract changes inside each changed nested repository, update root gitlinks, and record final SHAs and clean status.
system_actor_contract: The bound inventory identifies no autonomous production background mutation writer. api/document-api/app/tasks/index_knowledge_document.py and api/integration-api/api/integration.go are deferred continuations that must preserve their originating request actor and must not synthesize system identity. RAPIDA_SYSTEM_ACTOR_ID is startup-validated for any service that configures it, and registry tests prove active ownership, missing identity rejection, and wrong-owner rejection. Adding an autonomous writer requires returning to the RFC gate and naming its owned path.
service_assertion_contract: ValidateServiceIdentity requests actor ID, issuer, and key ID and returns only the matching active Ed25519 public key; ValidateSystemIdentity requests actor ID and owner and returns only active ownership. Producers sign assertions with RAPIDA_SERVICE_PRIVATE_KEY. At startup, each configured producer derives the Ed25519 public key from RAPIDA_SERVICE_PRIVATE_KEY and compares it with the active key returned by the registry; missing, malformed, or mismatched keys fail startup. Receivers parse routing claims without trusting them, retrieve the active public key from Web with a three-second timeout, then validate EdDSA signature, issuer, audience rapida-internal, iat, exp, kid, actor ID, and bigint range. Web uses the same verifier with a local registry implementation to avoid recursion. Registry unavailability and key rotation fail closed; prior-key tokens are rejected immediately.
service_rollout: Provision every service identity, active key ID, and Ed25519 public key in Web, and install the matching private key on each producer before code deployment. Fence internal service traffic; deploy Web registry RPCs first, then all receiving and producing services while the fence remains active; run one signed assertion smoke test per service; resume traffic only after every smoke test passes. For rotation, fence the individual producer, stop old-key traffic, replace its registry public key and deployed private key as one maintenance action, verify the new assertion, then resume; the old key has no overlap window.

migration_execution_contract: Each run migration is a single top-level CALL and contains no transaction wrapper. github.com/golang-migrate/migrate/v4/database/postgres v4.19.0 executes a migration through database/sql ExecContext without adding a driver transaction, permitting the procedure's COMMIT after each 10000-row batch. The verification script must run the real driver against PostgreSQL 16, interrupt after one committed batch, confirm 10000 rows remain converted, force the dirty run version back to the preceding definition version, rerun, and complete the full history.
sdk_drift_disposition: SDK-only AssistantAnalysis and AssistantWebhook proto copies retain reserved declarations for removed field names/numbers but expose no active createdBy, updatedBy, createdUser, or updatedUser fields. They are accepted as non-canonical compatibility records. The React widget has no protobuf source checkout and is validated against the generated React SDK through its own test and build commands.
migration_compatibility_evidence: The listed Phase 3 conversion, run, finalization, identity, and cleanup files are absent from git ls-files at amendment time, so no published commit or tag contains the superseded local numbering. Renumbering remains gated on a release/environment-owner receipt that no non-git environment applied the local drafts; without that receipt, shipping must stop and append-only corrective versions must replace the renumbered sequence.
rollback: Keep traffic fenced during conversion. A failed top-level CALL is forced back to the procedure-definition version and rerun, preserving previously committed batches. Before cleanup, actor-capable binaries may be rolled back while additive columns remain. Column removal is the irreversible boundary. After cleanup, restore all four same-point backups, deploy the previous complete binaries/contracts, pass legacy write/read smoke tests, and only then resume traffic.
